hyps.why: At very small learning rates the network is under-trained in 243 epochs, so increasing the rate helps a lot.
Rates near 0.278 and 1 make Adam unstable or divergent, so going higher hurts.
With a small learning rate, larger batches mean fewer updates, which worsens under-training.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training at aggressive learning rates.
Wider layers amplify update magnitude and instability when the learning rate is already large.
Deeper ReLU nets diverge or die more easily at high learning rates.
Alpha near 0.129 to 1 causes strong underfitting, so increasing it further hurts.
With a tiny learning rate, wider layers learn faster per step and add capacity.
Small batches combined with a large learning rate produce very noisy, unstable updates.
Tiny batches already give noisy updates, so a smaller learning rate stabilizes them, whereas large-batch configs need the larger rate.
